PullRequest.Title: chat: release hidden diff hunk toolbar listeners
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #260083.

### Cause and change

`DiffHunkWidget` eagerly creates a menu-backed toolbar for every hunk. Pooled widgets keep those menus and shared listeners alive even after their overlays are removed. Session disposal already releases them; this is excess live retention, not evidence of an unbounded post-disposal leak.

- Create a hunk toolbar when the hunk is revealed; release it when hidden or removed.
- Preserve widget pooling and the visible toolbar across stable-pool rerenders, avoiding the typing/focus regression from #274223.
- Let in-flight toolbar actions report completion before releasing their toolbar.
- Add regression coverage for real menu ownership, focus/node preservation, reuse, and action completion.

This does not change the generic `MenuWorkbenchToolBar`. The broad visibility approach in #312317 was reverted by #312669; #309287 and the pool-removal proposal #304152 were closed unmerged. Open `freeze-slow-crash-leak` PRs, including unlinked fixes, were checked for overlapping implementations.

### Validation

On current-main baseline `6d15fc6f79540b4600fd5aa7deed4d4524fccda6`, an actual Code OSS renderer with empty isolated profiles and deterministic local response progress reproduced the reported menu/hunk stack.

| 240-hunk workload | Main | This change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Hunk toolbar objects while one hunk is revealed | 240 | 1 |
| Hunk toolbar objects after accepting all, before ending the session | 240 | 0 |
| Shared menu listeners while rendering | 283 | 44 |
| Shared menu listeners after accepting all | 282 | 42 |
| Shared menu listeners after ending the session | 40 | 40 |

Original renderer heap snapshots corroborate object ownership and the strong shared-emitter -> menu -> toolbar -> widget path. Widget shells remain pooled intentionally.

- Two ownership tests fail on unmodified main; the existing stable-pool focus/node behavior passes.
- **51 targeted Electron tests pass** across the new integration suite, `ChatEditingService`, and modified notebook entries.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, targeted ESLint, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Actual baseline/candidate Code OSS checks pass: typing, mouse Keep, keyboard Undo, cursor/hover interaction, repeated model switches, diff/file toggling (#245110), accessible diff/Escape, AI-disabled hiding, last-hunk completion reporting, deleted notebook-cell controls (#277023), and notebook code-cell Keep/Undo.
- Two independent full-diff reviews (GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, default effort) found the same action-completion issue in the first candidate. It was reproduced, fixed, and both final follow-ups reported no remaining significant findings.

**Limits:** The adapter exercises real editor/chat lifecycle code, not authenticated Copilot/provider flows, and makes no model requests. No physical screen-reader or cross-platform claim. Existing FIFO pool rotation can change the active widget when spare widgets exist; node/focus preservation is limited to stable pool mapping. Full integration disposal during an action retains its existing immediate-disposal semantics. This does not claim to eliminate every aggregate menu-listener warning.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Eager per-hunk toolbar construction retained one menu, global menu/action-view subscriptions, action items, and toolbar DOM per pooled DiffHunkWidget until the entire editor integration was disposed, although only the active hunk toolbar was visible.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Renderer memory and shared-listener count grow linearly with the number of chat diff hunks and remain elevated across rerenders/removals for the session lifetime, increasing memory/GC pressure on large generated edits.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Toolbars are now created only when a hunk is revealed, preserved through its 200 ms fade and in-flight actions, and disposed when hidden or removed. Pooled widget shells remain, but their menu-backed toolbar resources no longer scale with all historical/current hunks.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, DiffHunkWidget constructed a MenuWorkbenchToolBar in every widget constructor. The render loop creates/reuses one DiffHunkWidget for every diff change and returns unused widgets to an ObjectPool whose free list survives render-store clears until integration disposal. MenuWorkbenchToolBar synchronously creates an IMenu, subscribes to menu/action-view changes, renders actions, and owns DOM. Thus a file with H hunks retained H menus, listeners, action items, and toolbar DOM for the editing session even though toggle() revealed only the cursor/hover hunk. The changed code moves construction into _showToolbar() and _hideToolbar() clears the toolbar store after fade/remove, so ownership tracks the one/few revealed or fading widgets.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or rerender a chat-edited file containing many diff hunks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor's diff autorun creates or reuses one lightweight DiffHunkWidget per hunk and lays each out before rendering can settle. After the change, menu-backed toolbar construction is off this collection-wide critical path except for at most the currently selected hunk revealed by the cursor autorun.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number H of effective diff changes after the document diff has grouped edits into hunks. The widget pool grows to the largest simultaneous H for the integration, while live toolbar/menu ownership now tracks revealed/fading hunks rather than H.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer/UI thread; hunk creation and layout are serial. No async fan-out or shared limiter is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: DiffHunkWidget shells are pooled and reused across rerenders. Before the diff, each cold widget eagerly created and retained a toolbar; warm rerenders reused those toolbar-bearing widgets. After the diff, pooled hidden widgets have no toolbar, a visible widget reuses its toolbar across stable-pool rerenders, and removed/hidden widgets dispose it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the render loop is explicitly per diff change, ObjectPool retains free widgets, and MenuWorkbenchToolBar creates an IMenu, listeners, action view items, and DOM. The changed lazy show/clear path removes that eager retained resource.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact bytes and listener cost per MenuWorkbenchToolBar depend on registered menu actions and context, but the old and new cardinalities are established directly by construction, pooling, and disposal ownership.
Scenarios.Verdict: This is a concrete performance fix, not a regression: retained menu/listener/DOM resources fall from O(H) for the session to O(revealed or fading widgets), normally one or two.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move the cursor or pointer between diff hunks to reveal toolbar actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cursor-position and mouse-move handlers synchronously scan hunk ranges, toggle widgets, create a toolbar on a cold reveal, update the hover class, and measure/layout the active overlay before the interaction completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Each pointer/cursor event still scans H widgets/ranges as before. New toolbar construction occurs once per reveal after that widget has remained hidden beyond the 200 ms fade; rapid re-reveal within the fade reuses the same toolbar.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer/UI thread. Fade cleanup uses one RunOnceScheduler per widget, but only widgets that transitioned from visible to hidden have scheduled callbacks; repeated hidden mouse events do not reschedule them.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The visible toolbar is reused while shown, through the 200 ms fade, and across stable pool rerenders. A reveal after cleanup is a cold toolbar creation; there is no global toolbar cache or cross-widget sharing because the menu argument is widget-specific.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for placement and cardinality; low for any user-visible latency regression because the bounded toolbar is small and no trace, benchmark, or established expensive boundary shows harmful duration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Lazy creation adds menu/action DOM construction and an immediate width/layout read to a cold reveal, but only for one toolbar and there is no repository evidence that this bounded work causes measurable input jank. Repeated warm navigation can recreate toolbars, but avoids retaining all hunk menus.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded cold-reveal work is an intentional scheduling tradeoff for eliminating O(H) retained menus, with fade reuse preventing churn during rapid hover transitions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hide, remove, disable, or pool a hunk toolbar during rerender/model changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A hide waits for the existing 200 ms opacity transition, while remove/pool/disable cancels that delay and synchronously clears the toolbar disposable store. These operations occur during renderer diff updates and model/review-mode lifecycle changes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Removal can touch up to H widgets serially, but each toolbar is cleared at most once and only revealed/fading widgets own one; hidden updates do not postpone cleanup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer thread. Scheduler cancellation and store clearing are serial; no cleanup fan-out crosses a process or service boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Widget shells remain in the pool for reuse. Toolbar state is invalidated on removal/disable and recreated only on the next reveal; integration disposal releases the pool and any remaining toolbar stores.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: remove cancels scheduling, _hideToolbar guards visible/running states, and DisposableStore.clear releases the MenuWorkbenchToolBar and subscriptions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Disposal cost depends on menu action count, but effective toolbar cardinality at removal is bounded to revealed/fading widgets rather than all H.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup-lifecycle regression. Cleanup is prompt on removal and bounded on fade, with no lost live resource handle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run Keep/Undo toolbar actions while the hunk hides, is removed, or its pooled widget is reused
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action executes through the existing ActionRunner. The changed code increments a local running count on will-run and defers toolbar disposal until on-did-run has notified listeners; a microtask then decrements the count and clears only if still hidden.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Retention scales with the number of concurrently running actions on revealed toolbars, not total H. Multiple actions on one toolbar share that toolbar and are counted; resolved actions release it once the count reaches zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Action promises may overlap without a new limiter, matching prior action concurrency. Disposal is coalesced by one counter per widget and occurs after all completions; the changed code introduces no subprocess/IPC/network concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A running toolbar is temporarily pinned even if hidden or pooled so its ActionRunner can finish notification. If the widget is revealed/reused before completion, that same toolbar is retained; otherwise it is released after the final completion. Full integration disposal remains immediate.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: onWillRun/onDidRun accounting and tests cover success, failure, concurrent actions, removal, reuse, and integration disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Downstream command implementations can perform unrelated work, but this diff neither adds nor moves those operations. Retention duration is action duration, and resource cardinality is bounded by concurrently active toolbar actions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Temporary retention preserves completion semantics and is bounded by in-flight action lifetime and concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. No diff-introduced performance finding met the reporting threshold. The production change fixes eager per-hunk menu/listener/DOM retention; the introducing commit was recorded via base-line blame. Cold toolbar creation is moved onto first reveal but is bounded and reused through the fade/stable rerenders, with no evidenced user-visible latency regression or expensive external boundary.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
